name: Retail shops and chains (general merchandise, multi-branch)

problems.words: Log shop mein aate hi nahi, footfall gir gayi hai
quick_ideas: Refresh each branch's Google Maps listing with current photos and hours, because many walk-ins start with a nearby search
Count walk-ins at the door by hand for a few days, so you know whether footfall is really down and at which hours.

workzap_build.text: regular WhatsApp messages to opted-in customers for each branch, each with its own branch code, so you see every week which message brought people into which outlet.

problems.ask_first: Is the drop at every branch or mainly one location?
problems.free_stops: Which messages, codes and timings per branch, and how visits are tracked back to them, are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk each branch frontage at busy time and note blocked signs, dark spots or closed-looking areas, so fewer passersby assume you are shut.
Give one person per branch the job of checking entrance appearance before peak hours, so the shop looks open when people pass.

problems.words: Log aate hain, dekhte hain aur bina khareede chale jaate hain
quick_ideas: Compare a week of hand-counted walk-ins against the number of bills, so you see which branch and hours lose browsers
Keep a sheet at the counter for items and sizes customers asked for but you didn't have, because the reason is often a missing piece rather than price.

workzap_build.text: a morning read per branch showing walk-ins against bills, basket size and the "asked for but not available" list, every day, side by side.

problems.ask_first: Do you have any count of how many people walk in each day?
problems.free_stops: How walk-ins and lost sales are captured at the counter and turned into the daily read is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the main item people ask for before leaving empty handed this week, so you spot what sends browsers back out.
Give one person each shift a single list for customer asks you could not serve, so missed demand reaches buying clearly.

problems.words: Every stock count, the main branch is short and nobody can explain it
quick_ideas: Count one high-risk category in the worst branch yourself, so you know whether the gap is concentrated or spread out
Check whether returns, damages and transfers out are written down, since many "shortages" are unrecorded movements.

workzap_build.text: short daily counts by category taken on a phone with photos, compared with recorded stock, with the gap tracked for each branch and category over time.

problems.ask_first: Is the shortage mostly in certain types of maal?
problems.free_stops: Which categories to count on which days, and how gaps are flagged, are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare shortages by category from the last few counts, so you see whether the main branch problem sits in one type.
Give one role the job of writing every return, damage and transfer on one page, so missing movements stop blurring counts.

problems.words: Maal godown se branch bhejte hain, branch kehti hai aaya hi nahi
quick_ideas: Match last month's transfer notes against what each branch says it received, so you see how big the gap really is
Ask the receiving branch to confirm the next few transfers the same day, so lost notes stop hiding the problem.

workzap_build.text: a request, dispatch and receive flow on phone where branches tick items in, and anything not received within a set time is flagged to you automatically.

problems.ask_first: Do transfers go with a paper slip today, or only by phone?
problems.free_stops: The transfer steps, who confirms what and the alert timings are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare dispatch notes with receiving notes for the last few branch transfers, so you see where handover details break.
Make the sender note branch, item and dispatch time in one transfer notebook, so warehouse and branch speak from the same record.

problems.words: Ek branch mein fast movers khatam, doosri mein dher laga hai
quick_ideas: Get every branch's count of just your top sellers on one day, so you see where stock is sitting
Move extra from the fuller branch before buying more, so cash isn't tied up in duplicates.

workzap_build.text: branch-level stock with reorder levels, an alert when a fast mover runs low anywhere, and a suggested transfer from the branch holding extra.

problems.ask_first: Is there a central godown, or does each branch buy for itself?
problems.free_stops: Reorder levels per item and branch, and how transfers are suggested, are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk both branches and note the same fast movers missing here but piled there, so rebalancing opportunities stand out quickly.
Give one person the weekly job of comparing fast movers across branches, so stock moves before one side runs dry.

problems.words: A whole room of stuff hasn't sold in a year
quick_ideas: List the dead stock by rough age once, so you know how much money is sitting there
Send some of it to a branch where similar items still sell, because a slow item in one area can move in another.

workzap_build.text: a dead-stock report by age and branch, refreshed automatically, with suggested transfers to branches where each item still sells.

problems.ask_first: Are these items barcoded or recorded anywhere?
problems.free_stops: The ageing rules and how transfer suggestions are worked out are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the dead stock room and note which categories take the most space, so the biggest blockage gets named clearly.
Give one person one notebook for dead stock moved out to branches or display, so this pile starts getting regular attention.

problems.words: Closing cash never matches the POS by a few thousand
quick_ideas: Count each drawer at shift change for a few days, so a gap points to a shift instead of the whole day
Separate cash, card and wallet totals on the closing sheet, so one doesn't hide another.

workzap_build.text: a daily closing entry on phone compared automatically with the POS, the gap logged per counter, shift and branch, plus days since each branch last deposited.

problems.ask_first: Is the gap usually the same branch or counter?
problems.free_stops: The closing steps, gap limits and deposit alerts are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare cash gaps by shift and day for one week, so you see when the mismatch usually starts.
Give one closing role one place to note cash received, paid out and handed over, so the count follows a clear trail.

problems.words: Managers give discounts to their own people
quick_ideas: Pull one month's POS discount report by branch, so you see patterns rather than suspicions
Write down who may give what discount, so managers know the rule exists.

workzap_build.text: an approval step for discounts above the rule, with voids, returns and discounts logged by counter and shift and alerts when one stands out.

problems.ask_first: Does your POS record who applied each discount?
problems.free_stops: The approval rules, thresholds and exception alerts are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which branches and days show the most discounts this month, so the pattern is discussed without naming anyone.
Give one role per branch the job of writing every special discount reason in one register, so exceptions stop blending into routine selling.

problems.words: Branch reports come a week late, each in a different format
quick_ideas: Decide the handful of numbers you need every morning, so branches know what matters
Ask all branches for those same numbers once this week, so you can compare them side by side for the first time.

workzap_build.text: one WhatsApp message each morning with yesterday's sales, cash vs card, top and bottom items and stock issues for every branch, with no one compiling it.

problems.ask_first: Do all branches use the same POS?
problems.free_stops: Which numbers go in the read and how they are pulled from each branch's system are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which parts of each branch report arrive late or missing this week, so the hold up is specific instead of general.
Set one fixed time daily for branch figures to be written in one shared format, so comparisons stop waiting a week.

problems.words: Har mahine naye cashier train karne parte hain
quick_ideas: Ask the last few people who left what pushed them, because the reason is often fixable
Pair the next new joiner with one experienced person, so training doesn't vary by branch.

workzap_build.text: onboarding and opening/closing checklists on WhatsApp with photo proof, so routines run the same at every branch whoever is on shift.

problems.ask_first: Which role is hardest to keep filled?
problems.free_stops: The checklists and how missed items reach the area manager are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which branch and shift each new cashier leaves from this month, so the churn pattern stops looking random.
Give one senior per branch the job of signing off cashier basics each evening, so training stays steady during frequent joining.

problems.words: People ask for online order and delivery and we have nothing
quick_ideas: Note how many people ask for delivery this week, so you know the demand is real
Share photos of your top items on your WhatsApp status each week, so customers can at least see and ask.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp, phone and online orders in one place, linked to branch stock and tracked to delivery.

problems.ask_first: Which cities would you deliver to first?
problems.free_stops: How orders flow from each channel to the right branch and to delivery is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many people ask for delivery and which items they mention this week, so you know what demand sounds like.
Keep one notebook near the counter for delivery requests and missed orders, so staff stop losing these chances between shifts.

never_say: That a specific cashier, manager or storekeeper is stealing, or how to watch staff secretly.
Anything about FBR POS integration rules, sales tax, VAT or keeping separate books.
Lease, rent negotiation or employment law advice.
That a listing, display or message will bring a certain number of customers or lift sales.
To confront or detain shoplifters; for threats or violence, contact the police first.

sample_reply.person: Hamari teen clothing branches hain, Tariq Road wali mein log aate hi kam hain, aur jo aate hain woh bhi dekh ke chale jaate hain. Koi solution batayein.
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, is ka hal mumkin hai, aur is ke liye bade kharch ki zaroorat nahi.
Pehle, tariq Road branch ki Google Maps listing naye photos aur sahi timing ke saath update karein, kyunke bohot log nazdeeki search se hi aate hain.
Doosra, kuch din darwaze pe aane walon ki ginti aur bills ki ginti mila ke dekhein, taa ke pata chale kis waqt log bina khareede jaate hain.
Workzap is se aage ye kar sakta hai: har branch ka subah ka report jis mein footfall, bills aur "maanga lekin nahi mila" ek jagah dikhe, aur customers ki ijazat se un ko branch code wale WhatsApp messages.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
